title: Mobile app and webview bridge
status: AUTHORED. The client behind the web app, and the trust boundary that is usually weaker than the web one.

atom_notes.A03: the app authenticates differently and often trusts the device
atom_notes.A05: the webview bridge passes typed data across a trust boundary
atom_notes.A06: deep links and intent filters are namespace surface
atom_notes.A08: the APK is a source of endpoints and keys no response reveals

required_cells.why: the package inventory is faster and richer than any black box probe
recovered client logic to hypothesis about hidden endpoints
runtime hooks are needed for pinning and for logic that is not in static code
the webview bridge is the exploitation surface
prove bridge reach with a control origin
retest after pinning or bridge changes

entries.name: jadx
entries.role: DEX to Java, the readable half of APK analysis

entries.name: apktool
entries.role: Manifest and resource decode, smali, and a rebuild path

entries.name: frida
entries.role: Runtime instrumentation, the only way to beat pinning and read logic at runtime
preconditions: a device or emulator you control
oracle: hook output showing the decrypted value or bypassed check
entries.note: frida.re did not resolve from the checking host. GitHub is the stable reference.

entries.name: objection
entries.role: Frida wrapper with ready made pinning and jailbreak bypasses
oracle: bypass applied and the app proceeding

entries.name: Mobile Security Framework
entries.role: Automated static and dynamic analysis with a report

entries.name: rea inspect_android_package
entries.role: Manifest, permissions, classes and resources without writing source to disk

entries.name: rea inspect_android_class / inspect_android_method
entries.role: Class members and a single decompiled method, plus reference tracing
preconditions: an APK and a class name

entries.name: rea decode_android_resources
entries.role: Readable AndroidManifest and string resources, the fastest way to find endpoints and keys

entries.name: blutter (Flutter AOT)
entries.role: Recover Dart symbols from libapp.so, the only way into an app whose logic is not in DEX
entries.note: Named as a gap in D31 and listed here as the tool that closes it. Not packaged, build from source.

entries.name: WeChat mini program unpacking
entries.role: The only route into a mini program's code, a China specific surface
preconditions: a .wxapkg package from a device you control
oracle: decompiled app service and page code
entries.note: No single canonical unpacker repo verified. Link goes to a GitHub search. Marked PROBABLE deliberately.

entries.name: OWASP MASTG
entries.role: The mobile testing guide, 240 section files, the closest thing to complete

entries.name: OWASP MASVS
entries.role: The requirement set, i.e. the fix side

entries.name: Atlas W05: file materialisation
entries.role: Technique pointer, W05 queued. Declared so the dependency is visible.
entries.note: Mobile technique depth belongs in the atlas. The pointer is honest about being queued.

tree.q: Do you have the package, or only a running app?
tree.why: Static gives you structure and a stable target. Runtime gives you values. Most people skip static and then fight pinning for an hour.

branches.action: decode, list exported components, extract strings, then find the API host and auth scheme
branches.oracle: endpoints and keys recovered from the package

branches.action: proxy it first. if pinned, hook the pinning check and retry
branches.oracle: requests visible through the proxy after the bypass

next.q: What can the loaded page call?

branches.action: enumerate the exposed methods, then test what they do with attacker controlled arguments and from an attacker controlled origin
branches.oracle: bridge method executed from an origin it should not accept

branches.action: test intent or URL handling for parameter injection and for reaching privileged screens
the logic is not in DEX. use the AOT or package specific tool first, or you will read nothing

mirror.detect: bridge call from an unexpected origin
mirror.control: allowlist origins and methods, validate arguments
pinning plus integrity checks, but assume bypass
